en: The national flower, Sampaguita, releases its sweet fragrance mostly at night to attract its specific moth pollinators.
National Scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate on mango trees induces them to flower even out of season.
The Ifugao maintain their rice terraces using muyong, a private forest management system where trees filter and regulate water flow.
The Philippine Eagle, our national bird, requires large, undisturbed dipterocarp forests to hunt monkeys and build its massive nests.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals preserve rice dough into kiping by drying it, a process that prevents microbial spoilage for months.
While exiled in Dapitan, Jose Rizal built a gravity-fed water system using local clay pipes to provide clean water to the town.
Narra, the national tree, is a deciduous species that drops its leaves during the dry season to conserve water.
The Badjao people read ocean currents and coral reef ecosystems to sustainably harvest sea cucumbers without damaging the marine habitat.
National Scientist Angel Alcala pioneered the establishment of marine sanctuaries to protect coral reefs and increase local fish populations.
The carabao, our national animal, wallows in mud to cool its body because it lacks functional sweat glands.
Baguio City hosts the Panagbenga flower festival because its high elevation creates a cool climate suitable for growing temperate plants.
Local government units use seismographs to monitor Mayon Volcano's seismic activity, predicting eruptions to protect nearby communities.
